key_insight: The paper defines semi-local wall coordinates and projected velocities through elliptic equations, so compressibility and wall heat-transfer effects are built into the transformation before extracting wall-normal profiles.
engineering_relevance: This gives a more physically consistent inner scaling for compressible wall turbulence, improving profile collapse and near-wall interpretation in high-speed boundary layers and channels with strong thermal asymmetry.
method: Build a semi-local wall coordinate from local density and viscosity scaling.
Solve a Helmholtz-type elliptic equation to add a bounded density-driven correction to wall-normal stretching.
Use projection equations to obtain transformed coordinate Y+ and projected velocity U+ from mean flow and wall geometry.
evidence_signal: A single calibrated set of wall-layer constants is tested on cooled flat plates, zero-pressure-gradient boundary layers, isothermal channels, and mixed thermal-wall channels, with improved inner and buffer-layer placement reported.
watch_item: The approach depends on solving elliptic equations with accurate mean density, viscosity, wall distance, and wall-normal data, so implementation cost and sensitivity to input-field quality are important.
paper_title: Semi-local transformation for compressible wall turbulence via elliptic equations
